what_this_is: The Phase 2 preregistration lock: the exact locked (peer, anchor-event) set, target definition, and model spec, fixed before any target/outcome value has been computed for any peer around any locked anchor event. See 'look_ahead_disclosure' below for exactly what has and has not already been touched.
what_this_is_not: Not a result, not the one locked run (a separate, later, not-yet-built module), and not permission to compute anything. It constrains what that later, separate, explicitly-authorized run may do; it performs none. No Phase 3 authorization has been drafted, requested, or signed for HYP-07 as of this lock -- that is a distinct, later, separately-authorized decision this document does not make.

target_definition.formula: signed_car(h) = sum_{i=t+1..t+h} (r_peer,i - beta * r_bench,i) - h * mean_{i in [ref_start, ref_end)} (r_peer,i - beta * r_bench,i). FIRST USE of a SIGNED target in this project -- HYP-04/05/06 all used target.py's magnitude-only realized-variance ratio instead. See target_signed.py's own docstring for the full derivation and provenance of each choice below.
target_definition.benchmark_beta_note: FIXED, never estimated -- the same anchor_shock.py AS-2 convention this project already uses on the anchor side, applied here peer-side. Choosing an estimation window after seeing how results move would be exactly the after-the-fact tuning this project's rules exist to prevent.
target_definition.return_basis: log, additive across days -- what makes a cumulative sum the natural signed analog of target.py's mean-based RVar ratio.
target_definition.residualization: NOT APPLIED. Deliberate v1 simplification, not an oversight -- target.EarningsCycleBaseline removes a MAGNITUDE confound (volatility rises into a company's own earnings) with no obvious signed analog for a cumulative abnormal RETURN. days_to_peer_earnings is still carried as a design-matrix control column. See target_signed.py's own docstring, 'DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED'.
target_definition.sign_convention: Nothing is flipped, anywhere: the anchor's raw SIGNED excess_return and the raw signed signed_car are used as-is. Significantly NEGATIVE peak beta confirms competitive displacement (anchor bad news, peer good news, and vice versa). Significantly POSITIVE peak beta indicates comovement/contagion instead -- the OPPOSITE of what a competitor relationship predicts, flagged explicitly as evidence the 'competitor' label may be picking up shared-sector/macro exposure, never silently relabeled as a confirming result. Not significant is a null, same reporting discipline as HYP-04/05/06.
target_definition.peak_horizon_caveat: target.py's RVar(h) is a MEAN over an expanding window -- later, unaffected days DILUTE it, so peak_horizon lands at the END of the true reaction window. signed_car(h) is a CUMULATIVE SUM instead -- it does not dilute, it PLATEAUS. Any HYP-07 result's peak_horizon must be read as 'where the cumulative effect saturates,' not the same geometric quantity HYP-04/05/06's own peak_horizon measures, even though both share the name. No code change follows from this -- inference.py stays correct exactly as written -- but every future report of a HYP-07 result must carry this disclosure.
target_definition.source: target_signed.py, hash-pinned above, first use of a signed target in this project.

model_spec.estimator: local projections with CR2 clustered standard errors, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, and max-T permutation multiplicity correction -- reused unmodified from inference.py/clustered_se.py, same as HYP-04/05/06.
model_spec.primary_cluster_key_note: Reused unchanged from HYP-05's own re-decision (clustered_se.HYP05_TWO_WAY_LIMITATION_NOTE), NOT re-decided for HYP-07 -- a project-wide method choice, not mechanism-specific. 195 locked events, each its own distinct (anchor, event_date) cluster.
model_spec.secondary_cluster_key_note: Reported via clustered_se.dual_cluster_report -- two ONE-WAY clusterings shown side by side, never a two-way estimator. The primary result above is HYP-07's actual inferential result; this is a robustness lens only.
model_spec.residualize_note: See target_definition.residualization above -- HYP-07's target has no residualization step of any kind, unlike HYP-04/05/06's required residualize=True.
model_spec.n_permutations_note: Reused unchanged from constants.py -- same values HYP-04/05/06 all used, not re-decided for HYP-07.

sample_size_disclosure.why: 195 locked (peer, event) pairs clears the provisional 195-pair floor -- but EXACTLY, not comfortably: the count and the floor are numerically identical, unlike HYP-06's own 778 pairs, which cleared the same floor by nearly 4x. Still framed exploratory, not confirmatory: the floor itself remains PROVISIONAL, and an even weaker borrow here than for HYP-06 (HYP-07's target is a different formula from the one the floor's k range was measured against) -- see HYP07_SAMPLE_SIZE_GATE_2026-09-13.md.

look_ahead_disclosure.already_touched: Every locked peer's raw close prices (auto_adjust=False) were fetched and used ONLY to compute point-in-time MARKET CAP for PS-1..PS-4 eligibility screening in run_hyp07_peer_market_cap.py. That computation never touched any peer's returns, signed cumulative abnormal return, or any quantity resembling this hypothesis's target measure. Relationship direction (competitor) was hand-verified from filing text during the round-7 review, which also never touches return data.
look_ahead_disclosure.not_touched: No log return, no signed cumulative abnormal return, and no beta has been computed for any locked peer around any locked anchor event, at any horizon, before this lock. This lock is written before that computation happens for the first time.

opens_no_gate: This is a computed HYP-07 Phase 2 lock, not a freeze, not a registry change, not a linkage ratification. It moves no gate condition, whatever the gate reads at the moment this file is read.
